velholdt.explanation: "Velholdt" means "well-kept", looking cared for and in good condition, such as a house, a garden or an old car. For a business that is managed well, use "veldrevet" (well-run): "en veldrevet butik" (a well-run shop).

sentence.da: Bilen er tyve år gammel, men meget **velholdt**.
sentence.en: The car is twenty years old, but very well-kept.

velkendt.explanation: "Velkendt" means "well-known", known by many people. It also means "familiar" when you know something well yourself, like a face or a tune.

sentence.da: Tivoli er et **velkendt** sted, som mange turister besøger.
sentence.en: Tivoli is a well-known place that many tourists visit.

velklædt.explanation: "Velklædt" means "well-dressed", wearing clothes that look good and suit the situation. It is built on vel (well) and klædt, from at klæde (to dress).

sentence.da: Han er **velklædt**, fordi han skal til et bryllup.
sentence.en: He is well-dressed because he is going to a wedding.

velkommen.explanation: "Velkommen" means "welcome". To greet guests, add "til" (to) before the place: "velkommen til Danmark" (welcome to Denmark). Do not use it for "you're welcome", which is "selv tak" or "det var så lidt" (it was nothing).

sentence.da: **Velkommen** til vores hjem!
sentence.en: Welcome to our home!

vellykket.explanation: "Vellykket" means "successful", said about something that turned out well, such as an event, a trip or an operation. It comes from "at lykkes" (to work out). For a person or company, say "succesfuld" (successful).

sentence.da: Festen var **vellykket**, og alle gik glade hjem.
sentence.en: The party was successful, and everyone went home happy.

velopdragen.explanation: "Velopdragen" means "well-behaved", about a child or a pet that has been raised to be calm and listen. It is built on vel (well) and at opdrage (to bring up).

sentence.da: Min hund er **velopdragen** og går pænt i snor.
sentence.en: My dog is well-behaved and walks nicely on a leash.

velsmagende.explanation: "Velsmagende" means "tasty", for food or drink that tastes good. It is built on vel (well) and at smage (to taste). In daily speech, people often say "lækker" (delicious) instead.

sentence.da: Suppen var **velsmagende**, fordi den var lavet af friske grøntsager.
sentence.en: The soup was tasty because it was made from fresh vegetables.

vemodig.explanation: "Vemodig" means "wistful" or "melancholic", a soft, quiet sadness mixed with memory, for example on a still autumn evening. It is gentler than "sorg" (sorrow).

sentence.da: Det gør mig **vemodig** at se gamle billeder af os.
sentence.en: It makes me wistful to see old pictures of us.

venlig.explanation: "Venlig" means "friendly" or "kind", for things such as people, voices and smiles. "Venlig hilsen" (kind regards) is how you end a letter or an email.

sentence.da: Hun er **venlig** og smiler til mig.
sentence.en: She is friendly and smiles at me.

venlighed.explanation: "Venlighed" means "kindness", being nice to other people: "Tak for din venlighed" (Thank you for your kindness).

sentence.da: Vi mødte stor **venlighed** på rejsen.
sentence.en: We met great kindness on the trip.

venligst.explanation: "Venligst" means "please" in a formal way and is common on signs and in letters: "Luk døren venligst" (Please close the door).

sentence.da: Husk **venligst** at lukke døren.
sentence.en: Please remember to close the door.

venstre.explanation: "Venstre" means "left", as in the left side or the left hand. In directions, you usually say "til venstre" (to the left).

sentence.da: Tag den første vej til **venstre**.
sentence.en: Take the first road on the left.

vent lidt.explanation: "Vent lidt" means "wait a bit". Add "tak" (thanks, please) to make it more polite: "Vent lidt, tak" (Wait a bit, please).

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter min taske. **Vent lidt**!
sentence.en: I'm looking for my bag. Wait a bit!

vest.explanation: "Vest" means "west": "Vinden kommer fra vest" (The wind comes from the west). It is also part of place names such as "Vestjylland" (western Jutland, the western part of the Danish mainland).

sentence.da: Solen går ned i **vest**.
sentence.en: The sun goes down in the west.

vestlig.explanation: "Vestlig" means "western" and also "from the west", as in a wind. For a part of a country, say "det vestlige" (the western part): "Esbjerg ligger i det vestlige Danmark" (Esbjerg is in western Denmark).

sentence.da: Vinden kommer fra en **vestlig** retning.
sentence.en: The wind comes from a westerly direction.

vestpå.explanation: "Vestpå" means "westward", toward the west, for movement: "Flyet drejer vestpå" (The plane turns west). For a place, use "vest for" (west of): "Esbjerg ligger vest for Odense" (Esbjerg is west of Odense).

sentence.da: Toget kører **vestpå** mod Esbjerg.
sentence.en: The train goes west toward Esbjerg.

vi.explanation: "Vi" means "we": "Vi bor her" (We live here). When "we" is the one being acted on, it becomes "os" (us): "Han ser os" (He sees us).

sentence.da: I dag spiser **vi** hjemme.
sentence.en: Today we eat at home.

vi ses.explanation: "Vi ses" means "see you" and is the everyday way to say goodbye. It is short for "we see each other". Add a time to be specific: "vi ses på fredag" (see you on Friday). In a more formal setting, use "på gensyn" (see you again).

sentence.da: Jeg skal gå nu. **Vi ses** i morgen!
sentence.en: I have to go now. See you tomorrow!

vi snakkes.explanation: "Vi snakkes" means "talk to you later" and is a casual goodbye between people who will speak again soon. It is common on the phone and in messages: "Tak for hjælpen, vi snakkes!" (Thanks for the help, talk to you later!)

sentence.da: Jeg har travlt nu, men **vi snakkes**.
sentence.en: I'm busy now, but talk to you later.

vi tales ved.explanation: "Vi tales ved" means "we'll talk" and is a friendly goodbye, mostly after a phone call or message, when you expect to speak again soon. Use "vi ses" (see you) instead when you expect to meet in person.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer i aften. **Vi tales ved**!
sentence.en: I'll call tonight. Talk soon!

via.explanation: "Via" means "by way of" or "through": "Vi kører via Odense" (We drive by way of Odense). You also use it for how you contact someone: "Skriv til mig via mail" (Write to me via email).

sentence.da: Vi rejser **via** København til Aarhus.
sentence.en: We travel via Copenhagen to Aarhus.

viden.explanation: "Viden" means "knowledge", everything a person knows about something. You say it without "a" or "the": "Viden er magt" (Knowledge is power).

sentence.da: Hun har meget **viden** om historie.
sentence.en: She has a lot of knowledge about history.

videnskabelig.explanation: "Videnskabelig" means "scientific", about research and knowledge gained with careful, tested methods. It is built on en videnskab (a science), which comes from viden (knowledge).

sentence.da: En **videnskabelig** undersøgelse bruger målinger til at finde svar.
sentence.en: A scientific study uses measurements to find answers.

vidtrækkende.explanation: "Vidtrækkende" means "far-reaching", about decisions and changes that affect many people or last a long time: "vidtrækkende konsekvenser" (far-reaching consequences).

sentence.da: Regeringens beslutning er **vidtrækkende**, og alle landets skoler bliver ramt.
sentence.en: The government's decision is far-reaching, and all the country's schools are affected.

sentence.da: Solnedgangen over havet var **vidunderlig**.
sentence.en: The sunset over the sea was wonderful.

vigtig.explanation: "Vigtig" means "important", for things such as objects, people, news and decisions. To say something matters to you, say "Det er vigtigt for mig" (It is important to me).

sentence.da: Søvn er **vigtig** for din krop.
sentence.en: Sleep is important for your body.

vikingetiden.explanation: "Vikingetiden" means "the Viking Age", the period from about 800 to 1050 when Scandinavian seafarers sailed, traded and raided abroad. It is built on viking (Viking) and tiden (the time).

forms.en: the ships of the Viking Age

sentence.da: I **vikingetiden** sejlede mange danskere til England og Irland.
sentence.en: In the Viking Age, many Danes sailed to England and Ireland.

vild.explanation: "Vild" means "wild": "vilde blomster" (wild flowers). In everyday talk it also means "awesome": "Den fest var vild" (That party was awesome).

sentence.da: Hesten var **vild**, men nu er den rolig.
sentence.en: The horse was wild, but now it is calm.

vild med.explanation: "Vild med" means "crazy about", for things and people you really like: "Jeg er vild med pizza" (I am crazy about pizza). It goes after "er" (am/is/are).

sentence.da: Min søn er **vild med** fodbold.
sentence.en: My son is crazy about soccer.

vildt.explanation: "Vildt" means "wild" when it describes an animal or a plant that lives free. In everyday talk, "Det var vildt!" means "That was crazy!", often in a good way.

sentence.da: En ræv er et **vildt** dyr.
sentence.en: A fox is a wild animal.

villig.explanation: "Villig" means "willing", ready to do something when asked. To name what you are willing to do, add "til at" (to) before the verb: "Hun er villig til at hjælpe" (She is willing to help).

sentence.da: Hun er **villig** til at vente lidt.
sentence.en: She is willing to wait a little.

villighed.explanation: "En villighed" means "willingness", being ready to do something when asked, without arguing. It comes from "villig" (willing).

sentence.da: Hendes **villighed** til at hjælpe gjorde os alle glade.
sentence.en: Her willingness to help made us all glad.

vind.explanation: "Vind" means "wind". To say it is windy, Danes use "at blæse" (to blow): "Det blæser" (It is windy).

sentence.da: Sejlbåden bruger **vind** til at sejle.
sentence.en: The sailboat uses wind to sail.

vindende.explanation: "Vindende" means "winning", describing what wins, such as a team or an idea in a contest. It can also describe a person or smile that wins people over: "et vindende smil" (a smile that charms).

sentence.da: Det **vindende** hold fik en pokal og tusind kroner.
sentence.en: The winning team got a trophy and a thousand kroner.

vindenergi.explanation: "En vindenergi" means "wind power", electricity made when the wind turns the blades of "en vindmølle" (a wind turbine). It is built from vind (wind) and energi (energy).

sentence.da: **Vindenergi** er ren energi, fordi den ikke forurener luften.
sentence.en: Wind power is clean energy because it does not pollute the air.

vinterbadning.explanation: "Vinterbadning" means "winter swimming", swimming in the sea in the cold months, often as a regular habit in a club.

sentence.da: Efter **vinterbadning** i det kolde hav varmer vi os i saunaen.
sentence.en: After winter swimming in the cold sea, we warm up in the sauna.

viral.explanation: "Viral" means "viral", spreading very fast online. It also means "caused by a virus": "en viral infektion" (a viral infection).

sentence.da: Videoen blev **viral**, og millioner af mennesker så den.
sentence.en: The video went viral, and millions of people saw it.

virkelig.explanation: "Virkelig" means "really" and makes a word stronger: "virkelig dejlig" (really lovely). Say "Virkelig?" (Really?) alone when you react to surprising news.

sentence.da: Maden er **virkelig** god.
sentence.en: The food is really good.

visdom.explanation: "Visdom" means "wisdom", the good judgment that comes from living and learning from mistakes, not from school. It is also in "en visdomstand" (a wisdom tooth), the last tooth to come in.

sentence.da: **Visdom** kommer med alderen, ikke fra bøger.
sentence.en: Wisdom comes with age, not from books.

visse.explanation: "Visse" means "certain" in the sense of "some, but not all": "visse regler" (certain rules). For just one thing, use "en vis" (with en-words) or "et vist" (with et-words): "en vis tid" (a certain time). Do not confuse it with "sikker" (sure), as in "Jeg er sikker" (I am sure).

sentence.da: **Visse** mennesker elsker kulde, men ikke alle.
sentence.en: Certain people love the cold, but not everyone.

vist.explanation: "Vist" means "probably" or "I think". Use it when you believe something is true but are not sure, and put it in the middle of the sentence: "Han er vist syg" (He is probably sick).

forms.en: I do not think we have milk

sentence.da: Han er **vist** hjemme nu.
sentence.en: I think he is home now.

vistnok.explanation: "Vistnok" means "apparently" or "I believe", used when you think something is true but are not fully sure, often because you heard it. It goes in the middle of the sentence: "Hun er vistnok hjemme" (She is home, I believe).

forms.en: He is coming tomorrow, I believe.

sentence.da: Han er **vistnok** flyttet til Aarhus, men jeg er ikke sikker.
sentence.en: He has apparently moved to Aarhus, but I am not sure.

vittig.explanation: "Vittig" means "witty", funny in a quick, clever way, usually about what someone says: "en vittig bemærkning" (a witty remark). Do not mix it up with "vigtig" (important): "Det er vigtigt" (It is important).

sentence.da: Han er **vittig**, fordi han altid finder et hurtigt, sjovt svar.
sentence.en: He is witty, because he always finds a quick, funny answer.

voksen.explanation: "Voksen" means "grown-up" or "adult". The same word also names the person: "en voksen" (an adult).

sentence.da: Når man er **voksen**, arbejder man.
sentence.en: When you are an adult, you work.

vold.explanation: "Vold" means "violence", using physical force to hurt someone. You say it without "en": "at bruge vold" (to use violence).

sentence.da: **Vold** er, når man med vilje gør andre fysisk ondt.
sentence.en: Violence is when you deliberately physically hurt others.

voldelig.explanation: "Voldelig" means "violent", about a person or an act that hurts others. For a storm, a pain or a reaction that is just very strong, Danes use "voldsom" (intense): "en voldsom storm" (a violent storm).

sentence.da: Han blev dømt, fordi han var **voldelig** over for sin nabo.
sentence.en: He was convicted because he was violent toward his neighbor.

voldsom.explanation: "Voldsom" means "violent" and "intense", about something with great force or size. It describes events and reactions, not a person who hurts others. For that, use "voldelig" (violent).

sentence.da: En **voldsom** storm rev tagene af husene.
sentence.en: A violent storm tore the roofs off the houses.

volleyball.explanation: "Volleyball" means "volleyball", the team sport played over a net. Like most sports, it takes the verb "at spille" (to play).

sentence.da: Vi spiller **volleyball** på stranden om sommeren.
sentence.en: We play volleyball on the beach in the summer.

vores.explanation: "Vores" means "our": "vores hus" (our house). It stays the same before every word, whether it is one thing or many: "vores børn" (our children).

sentence.da: **Vores** hus er meget stort.
sentence.en: Our house is very big.

vred.explanation: "Vred" means "angry". To name the person you are angry at, use "på" (at): "Jeg er vred på dig" (I am angry at you). For milder anger, Danes use "irriteret" (annoyed) or "sur" (grumpy).

sentence.da: Han er meget **vred** på mig.
sentence.en: He is very angry at me.

vred på.explanation: "Vred på" means "angry at". To name the person you are angry at, use "på" (at): "Jeg er vred på ham" (I am angry at him).

forms.da: Jeg er vred på mig selv.

forms.en: They are angry at each other.

sentence.da: Hun er **vred på** sin bror, fordi han løj.
sentence.en: She is angry at her brother because he lied.

vrede.explanation: "Vrede" means "anger", a strong feeling about something unfair. Say "Jeg er sur" (I am grumpy) about something small, and "vrede" about something serious, like a broken promise.

sentence.da: Folk følte **vrede**, fordi regeringen havde brudt sit løfte.
sentence.en: People felt anger because the government had broken its promise.

vrøvl.explanation: "Vrøvl" means "nonsense". It is blunt, so with someone you do not know well, say "Jeg er ikke enig" (I do not agree) instead.

sentence.da: Det er noget **vrøvl**, og jeg tror ikke på det.
sentence.en: That is nonsense, and I do not believe it.

våd.explanation: "Våd" means "wet", for clothes, hair, the ground, or anything with water on it.

sentence.da: Hunden er helt **våd** af regn.
sentence.en: The dog is completely wet from rain.

vågen.explanation: "Vågen" means "awake": "Er du vågen?" (Are you awake?) Do not mix it up with "at vågne" (to wake up): "Jeg vågnede klokken syv" (I woke up at seven).

sentence.da: Jeg er **vågen** hele natten.
sentence.en: I am awake all night.

væk.explanation: "Væk" means "away" or "gone". For movement: "Hun løber væk" (She runs away). For something you cannot find: "Min nøgle er væk" (My key is gone). "Gå væk!" (Go away!) sounds blunt because it is an order to leave.

sentence.da: Min taske er **væk**!
sentence.en: My bag is gone!

vækst.explanation: "Vækst" means "growth". It is the noun for the verb "at vokse" (to grow): "Planterne vokser hurtigt" (The plants are growing fast).

sentence.da: Virksomheden har haft stor **vækst** og ansætter nu flere folk.
sentence.en: The company has had big growth and is now hiring more people.

vældig.explanation: "Vældig" means "very" or "really": "vældig glad" (very happy), "vældig dejligt" (really nice).

sentence.da: Maden var **vældig** god.
sentence.en: The food was very good.

værd.explanation: "Værd" means "worth", for the value of something. To name what is worth doing, add "at" (to) before the verb: "værd at prøve" (worth trying).

forms.en: It is not worth the money.

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel er ikke mange penge **værd**.
sentence.en: The old bike is not worth much money.

værdifuld.explanation: "Værdifuld" means "valuable", for things worth a lot, in money or in meaning. It is built from værdi (value) and fuld (full). The same ending is in "smertefuld" (painful, literally "full of pain").

sentence.da: Den gamle ring er meget **værdifuld**.
sentence.en: The old ring is very valuable.

værdig.explanation: "Værdig" means "worthy" and also "dignified", calm and with self-respect. To name what the person deserves, add "til" (of): "værdig til respekt" (worthy of respect).

sentence.da: Hun er en **værdig** vinder, fordi hun har trænet i årevis.
sentence.en: She is a worthy winner because she has trained for years.

værdighed.explanation: "En værdighed" means "dignity", a calm pride in who you are, shown in how you carry yourself, even in a hard time.

sentence.da: Han tabte sagen, men forlod retten med **værdighed**.
sentence.en: He lost the case, but left the court with dignity.

værdiløs.explanation: "Værdiløs" means "worthless", with no value, in money or in use. It is built from værdi (value) and løs (without), and "løs" works the same in many words: "hjælpeløs" (helpless), "søvnløs" (sleepless).

sentence.da: Aktien er **værdiløs**, fordi firmaet er gået konkurs.
sentence.en: The share is worthless because the company has gone bankrupt.

værdsat.explanation: "Værdsat" means "appreciated", seen as valuable and respected for your work or your character. It comes from the verb "at værdsætte" (to appreciate).

sentence.da: Hun føler sig **værdsat**, fordi chefen takker hende hver uge.
sentence.en: She feels appreciated because her boss thanks her every week.

værre.explanation: "Værre" means "worse" and is the step up from "dårlig" (bad). It also appears in "et værre rod" (quite a mess).

sentence.da: I dag er det **værre** end i går.
sentence.en: Today it is worse than yesterday.

værsgo.explanation: "Værsgo" means "here you go" when you hand someone something, and "go ahead" when you invite them to do something. The reply is usually "tak" (thanks). If someone thanks you, say "selv tak" (you're welcome).

forms.en: Here you go, here is your coffee.

sentence.da: Må jeg låne din pen? **Værsgo**!
sentence.en: May I borrow your pen? Go ahead!

værst.explanation: "Værst" means "worst" and is the step up from "værre" (worse), which comes from "dårlig" (bad).

sentence.da: Vejret er **værst** i januar.
sentence.en: The weather is the worst in January.

væsentlig.explanation: "Væsentlig" means "significant" and "essential", about the part of a matter that really counts. You say it about a point or a difference: "Det er ikke væsentligt, hvem der vinder" (It does not matter who wins). For a person, say "vigtig" (important): "en vigtig person" (an important person).

sentence.da: Der er en **væsentlig** forskel på de to tilbud.
sentence.en: There is a significant difference between the two offers.

en webshop.explanation: "En webshop" means "an online store", a store you use on the internet instead of walking into a building. The word comes straight from English.

sentence.da: Jeg bestilte skoene i en **webshop** i går.
sentence.en: I ordered the shoes from an online store yesterday.

en webside.explanation: "En webside" means "a web page", one page on the internet. A whole site is often "en hjemmeside" (a website): "Firmaets hjemmeside er ny" (The company's website is new).

sentence.da: Jeg fandt en god **webside** om Danmark.
sentence.en: I found a good web page about Denmark.

en weekend.explanation: "En weekend" means "a weekend". Say "i weekenden" (on the weekend). On Fridays, Danes say "God weekend!" (Have a good weekend!).

sentence.da: Lørdag og søndag er en **weekend**.
sentence.en: Saturday and Sunday are a weekend.

en weekendtur.explanation: "En weekendtur" means "a weekend trip". It is built from weekend and tur (trip), the same tur as in "en biltur" (a car trip).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **weekendtur** til Berlin.
sentence.en: We are going on a weekend trip to Berlin.

en whisky.explanation: "En whisky" means "a whiskey", and also one serving of it: "Vil du have en whisky?" (Would you like a whiskey?) Without "en" it is the drink itself, not one serving: "Jeg kan godt lide whisky" (I like whiskey).

sentence.da: En **whisky** er en stærk drik lavet af korn.
sentence.en: A whiskey is a strong drink made from grain.

en wrap.explanation: "En wrap" means "a wrap", a soft flatbread rolled around a filling. For the bread alone, use "en tortilla" (a tortilla).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg en **wrap** med kylling og salat.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat a wrap with chicken and salad.

et whiteboard.explanation: "Et whiteboard" means "a whiteboard", a board you write on with markers and wipe clean. The older kind you write on with chalk is "en tavle" (a blackboard).

sentence.da: Læreren skriver nye ord på et **whiteboard**.
sentence.en: The teacher writes new words on a whiteboard.

et wienerbrød.explanation: "Et wienerbrød" means "a Danish pastry", a flaky sweet pastry from the bakery. The plural looks the same: "to wienerbrød" (two Danish pastries).

sentence.da: Jeg køber et **wienerbrød** hos bageren.
sentence.en: I buy a Danish pastry at the bakery.

wifi.explanation: "Wifi" means "wifi", the wireless connection you find in cafés, hotels and homes.

sentence.da: Hvad er koden til **wifi**?
sentence.en: What is the code for the wifi?

wow.explanation: "Wow" means "wow", a word for being impressed. To describe how impressive a person is, put "hvor" (how) after it: "Wow, hvor er han hurtig!" (Wow, how fast he is!)

sentence.da: **Wow**, hvor er det flot!
sentence.en: Wow, how beautiful it is!

at yde.explanation: "At yde" means "to provide" or "to perform", for help, support or effort that you offer: "yde støtte" (provide support), "yde en indsats" (make an effort).

sentence.da: Kommunen skal **yde** hjælp til familier i nød.
sentence.en: The municipality must provide help to families in need.

at ytre.explanation: "At ytre" means "to express" or "to utter": you say an opinion or a wish out loud: "Hun ytrer sin mening" (She voices her opinion).

sentence.da: Alle må gerne **ytre** deres mening i et frit land.
sentence.en: Everyone may express their opinion in a free country.

en yderside.explanation: "En yderside" means "an outside", the outer surface of something. The opposite is "en inderside" (an inside).

sentence.da: Vi maler husets **yderside** i dag.
sentence.en: We are painting the outside of the house today.

en yndlingsbog.explanation: "En yndlingsbog" means "a favorite book". The start "yndlings-" means "favorite" and works in many words: "min yndlingsmad" (my favorite food).

sentence.da: Jeg har læst min **yndlingsbog** mange gange.
sentence.en: I have read my favorite book many times.

en yndlingsfarve.explanation: "En yndlingsfarve" means "a favorite color". It is built from yndling (favorite) and farve (color). The same works for food: "min yndlingsmad" (my favorite food).

sentence.da: Min **yndlingsfarve** er grøn, og min søsters er blå.
sentence.en: My favorite color is green, and my sister's is blue.

en yndlingsfilm.explanation: "En yndlingsfilm" means "a favorite movie". The start "yndlings-" means "favorite" and works in many words: "min yndlingsmad" (my favorite food).

sentence.da: Min **yndlingsfilm** er meget gammel, men jeg elsker den.
sentence.en: My favorite movie is very old, but I love it.

en yndlingsret.explanation: "En yndlingsret" means "a favorite dish". It is built from yndling (favorite) and ret (dish). The word "ret" can also mean a court of law: "Han skal for retten" (He has to go to court).

sentence.da: Min **yndlingsret** er pandekager med syltetøj.
sentence.en: My favorite dish is pancakes with jam.

en yndlingssang.explanation: "En yndlingssang" means "a favorite song". The start "yndlings-" means "favorite" and works in many words: "min yndlingsmad" (my favorite food).

sentence.da: Jeg synger min **yndlingssang** i bilen.
sentence.en: I sing my favorite song in the car.

en yogamåtte.explanation: "En yogamåtte" means "a yoga mat", the soft mat you stand or sit on to do yoga. It is built from yoga and måtte (mat).

sentence.da: Hun ruller sin **yogamåtte** ud og laver yoga.
sentence.en: She rolls out her yoga mat and does yoga.

yderligere.explanation: "Yderligere" means "further" and "additional", on top of what is already there. You can also put it after a verb: "Priserne steg yderligere" (Prices rose even more).

sentence.da: Hvis du har **yderligere** spørgsmål, kan du ringe til os.
sentence.en: If you have further questions, you can call us.

yderst.explanation: "Yderst" means "extremely" and also "outermost", the part farthest out: "yderst til venstre" (on the far left).

forms.en: at the very end of the line

sentence.da: Det er **yderst** vigtigt, at du kommer til tiden.
sentence.en: It is extremely important that you arrive on time.

ydmyg.explanation: "Ydmyg" means "humble", not acting as if you are better than others, and ready to admit when you do not know something. It can also describe simple things: "en ydmyg bolig" (a humble home).

sentence.da: Vinderen var **ydmyg** og takkede alle, der havde hjulpet hende.
sentence.en: The winner was humble and thanked everyone who had helped her.

ydre.explanation: "Ydre" means "outer", for the part of something that is farthest out.

sentence.da: Husets **ydre** mure er hvide.
sentence.en: The outer walls of the house are white.

ymer.explanation: "Ymer" means "a Danish soured milk", thick and sour and usually eaten at breakfast. It is traditionally topped with "ymerdrys", a crunchy mix of dried rye bread crumbs and sugar.

sentence.da: **Ymer** er sur og tyk, og man spiser den med en ske.
sentence.en: Ymer is sour and thick, and you eat it with a spoon.

yndlings-.explanation: "Yndlings-" means "favorite". To make a "favorite" word, write it together with the word: "yndlingsmad" (favorite food), "yndlingsfarve" (favorite color).

sentence.da: Min **yndlings**farve er blå.
sentence.en: My favorite color is blue.

yngre.explanation: "Yngre" means "younger". It is the step up from "ung" (young): "Jeg er yngre end min bror" (I am younger than my brother).

sentence.da: Min søster er **yngre** end mig.
sentence.en: My sister is younger than me.

yngst.explanation: "Yngst" means "youngest", the one with the lowest age in a group. For two people, use "yngre" (younger): "Jeg er yngre end min bror" (I am younger than my brother).

sentence.da: Anna er **yngst** af mine børn.
sentence.en: Anna is the youngest of my children.

ynkelig.explanation: "Ynkelig" means "pathetic", so weak or poor that people feel pity or scorn.

sentence.da: Det var en **ynkelig** præstation, og holdet tabte stort.
sentence.en: It was a pathetic performance, and the team lost by a lot.

yoga.explanation: "Yoga" means "yoga", exercise with slow movements and calm breathing. To say you do it, use "at lave" (to do) or "at dyrke" (to practice).

sentence.da: I **yoga** strækker man sig og trækker vejret dybt.
sentence.en: In yoga, you stretch and breathe deeply.

yoghurt.explanation: "En yoghurt" means "a yogurt", one pot of it. For yogurt as a food, say "noget yoghurt" (some yogurt).

sentence.da: **Yoghurt** er lavet af mælk.
sentence.en: Yogurt is made of milk.

ytringsfrihed.explanation: "Ytringsfrihed" means "freedom of speech", the right to share your opinion without being punished for it. It is built from en ytring (a statement) and frihed (freedom), and it covers writing and publishing too, not only speaking.

sentence.da: **Ytringsfrihed** betyder, at alle må sige deres mening.
sentence.en: Freedom of speech means that everyone may say what they think.

en zebra.explanation: "En zebra" means "a zebra". In Danish the z sounds like an English s, so it is said SEE-bra.

sentence.da: En **zebra** har sorte og hvide striber.
sentence.en: A zebra has black and white stripes.
